# True or false: Measurement

DORA metrics, SPACE and the maturity model. Metrics help teams choose what to improve, and hurt them the moment they become targets for people.

10 statements (Foundation 5, Standard 5). Decide whether each one is true or false before you open the answer. Every answer says why and links to the page that teaches it.

Prefer the terminal? From the repository root, run `python3 exercises/quiz.py --area measurement`.

### 1. DORA metrics are a good way to rate individual engineers.

Level: Foundation

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** DORA metrics describe a system: a team, its tools and its process. The moment a metric becomes a target for people, it stops telling you the truth. Use the metrics to choose what to improve, never to rate individuals.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/metrics.md](../../playbook/measurement/metrics.md)

</details>

### 2. In DORA's research, teams that deliver faster also tend to be more stable.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**True.** Throughput and stability move together, so teams do not have to trade one for the other. Small, frequent changes are easier to review, test and roll back. That is why the playbook always pairs speed metrics with instability metrics instead of treating them as a trade-off.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/metrics.md](../../playbook/measurement/metrics.md)

</details>

### 3. DORA now tracks five software delivery metrics, including rework rate.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**True.** The five are deployment frequency, change lead time, failed deployment recovery time, change fail rate and rework rate. Rework rate is the share of deployments that are unplanned and caused by an incident in production. Failed deployment recovery time was formerly called mean time to restore.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/metrics.md](../../playbook/measurement/metrics.md)

</details>

### 4. The 2025 DORA report ranks teams as low, medium, high or elite, so every team should aim for elite.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** The 2025 DORA report replaced the low, medium, high and elite tiers with team archetypes. Do not set targets by copying a tier threshold. Set them against your own baseline, for example 'halve change lead time in 2 quarters'.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/metrics.md](../../playbook/measurement/metrics.md)

</details>

### 5. Ranking teams by deployment frequency helps the slower teams improve.

Level: Foundation

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** Teams work on different systems with different constraints, so a ranking mostly measures the context. It also invites gaming, such as splitting deploys to raise the count. Compare each team with its own baseline.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/metrics.md](../../playbook/measurement/metrics.md)

</details>

### 6. For a startup with no regulatory overlay, Foundation is the right target level in every practice area, including security.

Level: Foundation

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**True.** The levels are not grades. Foundation is the minimum that pays for itself immediately and is the default for solo engineers and startups. Assured adds evidence and separation of duties, which is worth its cost only where regulation, public accountability or real risk demands it.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/maturity-model.md](../../playbook/measurement/maturity-model.md)

</details>

### 7. In the self-assessment, you may answer true for a practice you plan to start next month.

Level: Foundation

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** An answer of true needs evidence that exists today. Answering on intent makes the report look better and the next actions wrong. Commit the answers to git and compare them each quarter.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/maturity-model.md](../../playbook/measurement/maturity-model.md)

</details>

### 8. Working on every gap the self-assessment finds at the same time is the fastest way to improve.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** Spreading effort across every gap means few of them close. The playbook works on at most 3 gaps per quarter, each with an owner. Reassess every quarter and pick the next ones.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/maturity-model.md](../../playbook/measurement/maturity-model.md)

</details>

### 9. No single metric captures developer productivity.

Level: Standard

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**True.** The SPACE framework (Forsgren and colleagues, 2021) describes five dimensions of productivity. Use at least three of them. Mix survey data with data from your systems.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/metrics.md](../../playbook/measurement/metrics.md)

</details>

### 10. Deployment frequency and lead time on their own give a fair picture of delivery.

Level: Foundation

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

**False.** Speed metrics alone reward shipping fast, even when changes break things. Always pair throughput with instability metrics, such as change fail rate and rework rate, and with SLOs. Together they show whether faster delivery is also safe.

Read more: [playbook/measurement/metrics.md](../../playbook/measurement/metrics.md)

</details>
